long_biography.plain_text:
Businessman Hamza Al-Kholi studied pharmacy at King Saud University and later funded a chair for developing medical education at Imam Muhammad ibn Saud Islamic University. The chair convened experts to set research priorities in curriculum, students, faculty and accreditation, and financed the publication of studies on medical training.

His university giving also extended to access for prospective students. At the American University in Cairo, he established an information centre where applicants and parents could learn about the campus and its programmes. His public-school scholarship enabled Egyptian students to attend the university; an early recipient hoped to use her education to improve schooling in rural communities.
